added_failures_note: a figure review runs no suite; no test was executed and no failure count was measured

findings.disposition: folded: nova:separatrix-spline-extraction s8 (redraw the DIII-D panels with the repository's 14 pt tick/legend and 16 pt axis-label sizes before the bank figures are treated as evidence)
findings.summary: The per-panel captions of frame_flux_comparison.png are drawn at fontsize=8, which is 10-12 px of ink on the 1400 px canvas and about 6 px in the ~900 px column the figure is read in. Those captions are the only place the figure states converged=False for all five frames and 'no closed branch; N candidate(s)', i.e. that no Nova separatrix exists in any panel. At the published column width the figure's central caveat cannot be read, so a reader sees a comparison of five fields and no statement that none of them converged.

findings.disposition: index-worthy: emit the legend entry only when a closed boundary was drawn, as the caption already reports the refusal
findings.summary: The legend advertises 'Nova separatrix' as a red line, but no red curve is drawn in any of the five panels: red ink measures 179 px in each of panels 1, 2, 4 and 5 and 0 px in panel 3, which is exactly the two red markers (axis triangle and X-point cross) and no curve. A reader is told a series exists that the picture does not contain.

findings.disposition: exempted: the extra-GPFS vacuum contours are the terminal current map the node exists to show; the comparison inside the boundary remains readable, so nothing is redrawn in this review
findings.summary: The Nova terminal-current psi contours are drawn over the whole display grid, so dense contour nests fill the vacuum region and the panel corners (3.2-4.3 thousand blue px per panel) and compete with the grey EFIT contours that carry the comparison. Clipping the Nova contours to the limiter would let the two fields be compared.

findings.disposition: exempted: fill (open vs filled) is a second cue, so the two X-points remain separable; no colour change is made in a read-only review
findings.summary: Nova axis, Nova X-point and Nova separatrix all resolve to the same colour (#cc0000: ink.axis_color, ink.xpoint_color and ink.separatrix_color are one value) and the two X-point markers share the 'X' glyph, so a reader must decode fill and shape together to tell the EFIT X-point from the Nova one.

findings.disposition: folded: nova:separatrix-spline-extraction s8 (same redraw as the frame comparison captions)
findings.summary: The per-panel captions of displacement_decomposition.png are also drawn at fontsize=8 (8-12 px of ink on the 1400 px canvas, about 6 px at column width). They carry the shot, frame, classification and the axis dR/dZ numbers, which are the quantitative evidence for the panels above them; the panels themselves remain readable, so this does not hold the node.

findings.disposition: folded: nova:separatrix-spline-extraction s8 (a table, or markers without connecting lines)
findings.summary: Five of the six panels of cohort_match_summary.png plot one scalar per frame and join the points with a line, across a categorical axis whose order (179, 44, 144, 146, 137) is arbitrary. Every segment implies a progression the data does not have, and the same five scalars are naturally a frame-by-metric table.

findings.disposition: folded: nova:separatrix-spline-extraction s8 (annotate the missing frame as the companion figures do)
findings.summary: Frame 144 is a silent gap in all five metric panels: no marker, no line, and no note. Measured on the rendered PNG, panel 1's plotting band holds no blue ink between x=200 and x=319, and the tick labelled 144 carries no value. The two companion figures label that frame 'unavailable: no qualified axis', so a reader of this figure alone cannot tell an unavailable frame from a zero or an omitted one.

findings.disposition: folded: nova:separatrix-spline-extraction s8 (label the threshold in the panel or the caption)
findings.summary: The grey dashed line at R2 = 1.0 in the first cohort panel is drawn with no label, legend entry or annotation, so nothing in the picture says it is the registered median interior-R2 bar the run is judged against.

cohort_match_summary.png draws its titles at 11 pt, axis labels at 10 pt and tick labels at 9 pt, against the repository's 16 pt axis-label and 14 pt tick-label sizes; at the ~900 px column width the frame ticks render about 8 px. Readable at native size, so this does not hold the node.

method: each figure judged only from its rendered PNG at 1400x720 px, 100 dpi; ink extents measured on the PNG pixels to check what the render actually shows before a verdict was recorded
